title: Round621: accelerated sampling backend feasibility
question: Would a JAX/GPU simulator materially accelerate our VGC search sampling, and is there a lower-cost exact simulator path to measure first?

target.format_rules: Local Champions Reg M-C doubles, Flat Rules, VGC Timer, ordinary species-visible preview, closed sets, six previewed and four selected.
target.reference: Local Showdown. It remains the correctness authority.

search_baseline.note: Elapsed search includes candidate work, state handling, transitions and value calls; it is not a pure simulator benchmark.

candidate_engine.name: Ninjask
candidate_engine.format_compatibility: Used its bundled Reg M-C Champions format data, removed only the Open Team Sheets rule, and assigned the local closed-sheet format id. The local format has the same battle mod, Flat Rules and VGC Timer; OTS changes information visibility, not turn mechanics.

local_showdown_parity_sample.method: Same packed teams, team preview, legal joint choices and sodium RNG seed were replayed in both engines. Player-view logs were normalized for timestamp, metadata, split lines and non-gameplay hints; turns, winner and remaining protocol events matched.
local_showdown_parity_sample.scope_limit: This is a small differential sample, not full-mechanics certification. The local Showdown checkout is not the same revision as Ninjask's pinned reference.

candidate_engine.hidden_choice_retry: In a separate 128-match probe, 125 replays matched and 3 initial choices were rejected by Showdown because of hidden trapping or Imprison effects. These require the same refreshed-request retry path already used by training; they were not engine outcome divergences.

matched_branch_benchmark.team_pair: Round595 development pool teams 24 and 0; team 1234 selected on each side.
matched_branch_benchmark.joint_actions: P1 Rock Slide plus Protect; P2 Fake Out plus Detect.

showdown.method: JSON snapshot parse, Showdown state deserialize, one joint turn advance

ninjask.method: Rust battle copy, reseed, one identical joint turn advance

matched_branch_benchmark.interpretation: This is a controlled one-turn branch microbenchmark, not a 206x full-search or training speedup. It isolates the transition/copy path and makes the CPU Rust backend a stronger near-term search candidate than starting a new JAX port.

chance_branching.scenario: Rock Slide across two targets with accuracy, damage rolls and flinch, plus opposing actions.
chance_branching.exact_enumeration: Both Precise and DamageEndpoints outcome enumeration exceeded a 200,000-path cap and took about 4.6 seconds to reach the cap in the tested state.
chance_branching.implication: Exact enumeration can still explode on the exact multi-target cases of concern. Fast controlled sampling remains necessary; the faster transition backend could make more samples practical.

jax_readiness.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, 8 GB; CUDA 13 driver available.
jax_readiness.jax: JAX 0.12.0.1 CUDA wheel ran in an isolated temporary environment. This confirms device compatibility only; no battle simulator has been ported or benchmarked on GPU.

decision: Keep Showdown as correctness authority. The CPU Rust candidate remains promising for sampling, but integrate only behind an optional backend that accepts player-view inputs, constrains choices using the acting player’s request, and retains Showdown differential checks. Do not expose Battle.projection() to policy/search features. Revisit a JAX port after an end-to-end Rust search comparison.

reproduction_notes.benchmark: 128 copies of the same selected local-Showdown state; one identical joint turn per branch; five trials; medians reported.
reproduction_notes.parity: 32 full seeded random-legal-choice matches against local Showdown; normalized player-view protocol logs and terminal result compared.

random_legal_choice_replay.filter: Remove switches when the acting player request marks the slot trapped or maybeTrapped; remove disabled moves.
random_legal_choice_replay.interpretation: The raw Ninjask legal-choice list is optimistic for some hidden trapping states. An adapter must intersect choices with the acting player request or handle server rejection and refresh; the raw list is not safe as a protocol action list.

closed_sheet_view_audit.phase: after team preview and four-Pokemon lead selection, before turn-one choices
closed_sheet_view_audit.result: Tracker.view did not change when only unrevealed opponent moves changed.
closed_sheet_view_audit.important_boundary: Battle.projection() includes hidden opponent moves, items, abilities, and stats; it is an engine snapshot and must never be passed to the agent. Tracker.view plus the acting player request is the candidate player-view interface.
closed_sheet_view_audit.scope_limit: This smoke check covers move secrecy in Tracker.view only; item, ability, stat, hidden roster assumptions, and every mid-battle event still need dedicated audits.
